prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 2.44. Exact Sanskrit: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥ Exact stored meaning: For those who are deeply attached to pleasure and power, whose minds have been carried away by such (flowery) speech — for them, the resolute, one-pointed understanding does not arise in meditation. Chapter context: Arjuna is distressed; Krishna teaches the Self, endurance, wise action and steadiness. For a described analogy, make that exact analogy the image. For abstract Self teachings, use a restrained interpretive natural scene or Krishna quietly instructing Arjuna; no invented literal body of the incorporeal Self. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Desirous of pleasures and heavenly reward, proclaiming rebirths as the fruit of actions, filled with various special rites aimed at attaining enjoyment and lordship — Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: The Vedas deal with the three guṇas (qualities of nature). Be free of the three guṇas, O Arjuna — free from the pairs of opposites, ever established in sattva, unconcerned with getting and keeping, and established in the Self. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.44: For those who are deeply attached to pleasure and power, whose minds have been carried away by such (flowery) speech — for them, the resolute, one-pointed understanding does not arise in meditation.
